question: The gas released on the reaction of metal carbonate with hydrochloric acid turns lime water milky. The released gas is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon Dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The reaction between a **metal carbonate** (e.g., calcium carbonate) and **hydrochloric acid (HCl)** produces **carbon dioxide (CO₂), water (H₂O), and a salt**. The general reaction is as follows:

 **Metal Carbonate + HCl → Salt + CO₂ + H₂O**.
 
• When the released **carbon dioxide gas** is passed through lime water (a solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂), it reacts to form **calcium carbonate (CaCO₃)**, which makes the lime water turn **milky**.

 **Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ (milky) + H₂O**.
 
• This reaction is a **qualitative test** for the presence of carbon dioxide gas.
